finding.claim: The DELETE handler calls the async authorize() without await. The 403 rejection is never awaited, so the delete runs regardless of the grant check. Any user can delete any report. The rejected promise is also unhandled, which can crash the process on newer Node versions.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sending DELETE /reports/:id with an arbitrary report id

trace.note: Report is loaded by the attacker-supplied req.params.id
authorize() is called without await, so the handler continues immediately
The grant lookup and the 403 throw happen inside the async function, after the caller has moved on

finding.guards_checked: authorize() would block the request if it were awaited; the PUT handler at line 27 does await it, which shows the intended pattern. No other middleware checks permissions. The only middleware (lines 4-7) just copies the session user into req.user and does not enforce any check.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws 403 when grant is missing, but it is called without await at line 20, so the throw doesn't stop line 21. The middleware at lines 4-7 only copies the session user and enforces nothing. The PUT handler awaits it at line 27, which is the correct pattern.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls async authorize() without await, so its 403 throw at server.js:14 becomes an unhandled rejection and server.js:21 db.reports.remove() runs anyway, letting any session user delete any report.

finding.claim: The PUT handler passes the raw request body to db.reports.update with no field allowlist. A user with only 'write' grant can overwrite any field on the report, such as owner or id. This is mass assignment, and its impact depends on the schema, which is not visible in this repo.
finding.source: JSON body of PUT /reports/:id from a user holding the 'write' grant

trace.note: The authorization check only verifies the 'write' grant on the report
The entire body is passed to update

finding.guards_checked: No schema validation or field filtering is present. The db module is not defined in this repo, so I could not confirm which fields are sensitive. This candidate is lower confidence than F1.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:27 is awaited and throws 403 without a 'write' grant, so it blocks users who lack the grant. Nothing filters req.body (server.js:28).
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (server.js:3, 27 and 28) and a user with only a 'write' grant can send an arbitrary body to db.reports.update at server.js:28, but db is not defined in this repo, so it is unknown whether update restricts fields or whether owner/id are sensitive.
